description: Machine-readable inventory of the deliberate accessibility problems in the original Record a goose sighting exercise. It is deliberately separate from the ACT fixture manifest: most of these problems do not map to an approved ACT rule.

counts.note: The answer key originally said 19 issues but enumerated 18. The nineteenth entry, start-image-filename-alt, was added deliberately and the answer page now lists all 19.

evidence.assertion: The page contains two h1 elements; the second is the related-links heading.

automated.note: No axe rule flags duplicate h1 elements.

manual.test: Open the headings list and compare the outline with the visible structure.

detection.whyMissed: The DOM is valid and every heading has text; judging whether two h1s make sense is contextual.

issues.title: Related links appear in a different order to the DOM

evidence.assertion: CSS order values are 1, 3, 2 while the DOM and Tab order are Wikipedia, More, RSPB.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the related links in a different visual order to the DOM

automated.note: CSS order is not part of the accessibility tree.

manual.test: Tab through the related links and compare the focus order with the visual order.

detection.whyMissed: Tools read DOM order; they do not notice that the rendered order differs.

issues.title: External link opens a new tab without warning

evidence.assertion: The RSPB link has target=_blank and its accessible name gives no advance warning.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps an external link that opens a new tab without warning

manual.test: Activate the RSPB link and check whether the new tab was announced in advance.

detection.whyMissed: Whether a new tab is expected depends on the link text and the user context.

evidence.assertion: The link's accessible name is exactly 'More' and only makes sense from the surrounding section.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the ambiguous "More" link text

automated.note: The link has non-empty text, so automated name checks pass.

manual.test: Read the links list out of context and decide whether "More" is meaningful.

detection.whyMissed: Automation can test that a name exists, not whether it is useful.

issues.title: Related links lose their focus indicator

evidence.assertion: Focused a.link elements have outline:none and a transparent background.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the invisible focus indicator on the related links

automated.note: No axe rule evaluates whether the focus indicator is visible.

manual.test: Focus each related link and look for a visible indicator.

detection.whyMissed: Focus visibility is a rendering outcome; the CSS deliberately removes outline and background.

evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the empty page title

automated.note: A missing title is a standard automated check.

manual.test: Listen to the page title announcement when the page loads.

evidence.assertion: The fieldset contains no legend and the question sits outside it.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the empty radio group legend

automated.note: The fieldset exists but has no legend; automated grouping checks do not treat this as a failure.

manual.test: Navigate to the radio group and listen for its group label.

detection.whyMissed: The radio buttons are individually named; the missing group name only appears in the interaction.

issues.title: Continue button removed from sequential focus

evidence.assertion: The submit button has tabindex=-1 and is never reached by Tab.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the Continue button out of sequential keyboard focus

automated.note: tabindex=-1 is valid and is used legitimately for programmatic focus.

manual.test: Tab from the radios and try to reach Continue without using the mouse.

detection.whyMissed: Automated checks test attributes in isolation, not whether every control is keyboard reachable.

evidence.assertion: Hint colour is rgb(157, 157, 161) on white; contrast is below 4.5:1.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the low-contrast hint text

automated.note: Contrast is measurable when colours are resolvable.

manual.test: Compare the hint with the background and confirm the ratio.

issues.title: Page title is 'Boop - Record a goose sighting'

evidence.assertion: The title contains 'Boop' and does not describe the page question.

automated.note: document-title only checks that a title is present.

manual.test: Read the title aloud and decide whether it describes this page.

detection.whyMissed: The title is non-empty but meaningless; usefulness is a judgement.

evidence.assertion: The visually hidden paragraph has tabindex=0 and is the second Tab stop.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the focusable, visually hidden ghost goose

automated.note: No rule pairs tabindex=0 with visually hidden text.

manual.test: Tab from the page start and observe focus disappearing onto "Ghost goose".

detection.whyMissed: The element is valid; the problem is where focus goes and what the user can see.

issues.title: Formatting hint only available as placeholder text

evidence.assertion: The input has a placeholder and no persistent hint or aria-describedby.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the placeholder as the only formatting instruction

automated.note: A placeholder is not itself a failure.

manual.test: Type a value and check whether the formatting guidance is still available.

detection.whyMissed: Tools cannot know that the placeholder is the only instruction.

issues.title: Change links use incorrect visually hidden text

evidence.assertion: Visually hidden text reads 'biscuits' and 'cake' instead of the field being changed.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the incorrect visually hidden Change-link text

automated.note: Visually hidden text exists and is non-empty.

manual.test: Read each Change link in the links list and check what it changes.

detection.whyMissed: Accuracy of hidden text is a content judgement, not a structural rule.

issues.title: Heading level jumps from h1 to h3

evidence.assertion: The first two heading levels are 1 then 3.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the incorrect heading hierarchy

automated.note: Skipped heading levels are checked by axe-based tools such as Accessibility Insights Fast Pass.

manual.test: Check the heading outline for a jump from h1 to h3.

evidence.assertion: The confirmation heading is literally 'GOOSE RECORDED'.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the uppercase confirmation heading

automated.note: Text in capitals is valid content.

manual.test: Read the confirmation heading and ask whether the capitals slow reading.

detection.whyMissed: This is a readability judgement rather than a rule violation.

evidence.assertion: The paragraph computes to text-align: justify.

manual.test: Read the paragraph and look at the uneven word spacing.

detection.whyMissed: Justification is a typographic outcome that depends on the rendered line lengths.

issues.title: Animated GIF has no alternative text

evidence.assertion: The confirmation image has no alt attribute and axe reports image-alt.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the animated GIF without alternative text

automated.note: A missing alt attribute is a standard automated failure.

manual.test: Listen to the image announcement on the confirmation page.

issues.title: Animation cannot be paused or stopped

evidence.assertion: The looping GIF has no pause, stop or hide control.

automated.note: No rule checks whether a looping GIF can be paused.

manual.test: Watch the page for more than five seconds and look for a pause or stop control.

detection.whyMissed: The animation is an image; control availability is not part of its markup.

issues.title: Image alternative is a file name

evidence.assertion: The start-page illustration uses alt="goose-illustration.svg", which names the file rather than describing the image.
evidence.test: tests/accessibility-regression.spec.js: keeps the start illustration with a file-name alternative

automated.note: A non-empty alt passes image-alt checks; automation does not judge whether it is equivalent.

manual.test: Listen to the start-page illustration in a screen reader and compare the announcement with the visible scene.

detection.whyMissed: Automation can confirm that an alternative exists, not that it describes the image.
